answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, a vendor switch (despite memory_c2's cost win) adds onboarding and delivery risk in a 14-day window; deferral (memory_c5) forfeits leverage and leaves the contract expired. Renegotiating at renewal (memory_c4) uses benchmark pressure to pursue the mandated 18% cut while preserving the stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries documented in memory_c1, possibly with a multi-year structure per memory_c6. I verify memory_c2 and memory_c4 because the decision hinges on whether the low-cost switch's savings and the renegotiation's margin recovery were as clean as the consolidated summaries claim.
